newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares firm 0.62 pct despite political fears.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares firm 0.62 pct despite political fears.

text.p: Istanbul shares firmed on Friday after Turkish Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller denied a press report that she would pull out of the Islamist-led coalition, brokers said.
But they said worries about the future of the government persisted as the market awaited Saturday's National Security Council (NSC) meeting to set direction next week.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,466, up nine points, or 0.62 percent from Thursday when it sank 4.9 percent following a 6-1/2 day holiday.

"Official statements on the continuation of the government enlivened activity slightly in the afternoon. But the market trend depends on the results of the NSC meeting," said Koray Cervatoglu from Baran securities.
The index had eased 0.21 percent to 1,454 in the morning.
"Don't believe things about withdrawing from the government that you haven't heard from me," Ciller told reporters after a leadership meeting of her conservative True Path Party (DYP).
A Turkish daily quoted on Friday unnamed cabinet ministers as saying Ciller had decided to pull her DYP out of the 10-month-old coalition.
The DYP is uneasy due to Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's failure to implement an anti-Islamist crackdown demanded by the secularist army at a February 28 NSC meeting.

Erbakan and the army have been at loggerheads since that meeting where the generals demanded measures to curb rising Islamist zeal. The government has taken no concrete steps to comply with the army's demands.
Trade volume firmed to 13.02 trillion lira from Thursday's 12.93 trillion.

Of the 248 shares traded, rises outdid falls by 100 to 72 and 76 finished stable. The IMKB Industrial firmed 0.62 percent to 1,464, the IMKB Services gained 0.81 percent to 1,376 and the IMKB Financial edged 0.57 percent higher to 1,580.
Leading actives were commercial vehicle venture Anadolu Isuzu, steady at 76,000 lira and state owned Turkish Airlines, up 3,500 lira at 34,000. They made up 17.5 percent of the total turnover.
